scope.description: Whole imagej application/library breadth across useful functional families.
scope.denominator: Image import/processing, filtering, segmentation, measurement, colour/stacks, ROI management, plugins and scientific visualisation.

coverage.rationale: The existing particle pipeline now also supports repeated named rectangular regions across declared grayscale frames. Both remain bounded measurement workflows; general image processing, segmentation, plugins and scientific visualisation are absent, so the coarse whole-application estimate remains 5%.

scope.description: Calibrated grayscale threshold-particle measurements or repeated named rectangular-region measurements across labelled frames, with explicit frame times and a typed workbook handoff.
scope.denominator: User intent and domain decisions within the named supported workflows, including declared inputs, composition and useful outputs; excluded application features do not enter this score.

abstraction.rationale: Calibration, threshold/connectivity, particle-size intent and named frame/region/time decisions hide Java and ImageJ measurement plumbing. Users still define rectangular regions and measurement assumptions; the existing 80% estimate is retained within this measurement family.

limitations: Closed bounded grayscale TIFF/PGM inputs. Repeated regions have explicit rectangles, frame times and common calibration; this is not object tracking, registration, segmentation, ROI-set import, colour processing or Fiji/plugin automation.

Pixel values, counts and geometric calibration are checked within the declared rectangle workflow. Authored calibration/time and biological meaning are not independently established by those checks; observed jar hashes establish consistency rather than publisher authenticity.

Frame dimensions/depth, aggregate pixel/byte/visit budgets and source alias constraints are enforced. Fractional means and nonunit calibrated areas remain numeric observations, with no uncertainty or acquisition-quality certificate.
Subjective source-contract assessment, not an exhaustive native API measurement. Verification confidence, runtime availability and source-bound qualification remain separate.
